title: Operations (logistics, finance, planning)

grammar.note: No grammar module yet. This family is the designed target; requires Z3 backend first.

why_verify: Enterprise decisions (ship via X, approve budget Y, schedule Z) are discrete satisfiability problems: the agent must pick an assignment satisfying every hardcoded rule (deadline, budget cap, hazmat compatibility, warehouse serves destination). A wrong pick is a real loss, and agents cannot be trusted to self-report compliance.
how_handled_now: Business-rule engines, manual review, and post-hoc auditor checks. All verify a human's or agent's claim after the fact, or enforce a policy in isolation — none proves across a conjunction of typed preconditions with an auditable trace, and none explains *which* rule was violated when one fails.
needs_before_ship: Z3 backend hook 'z3.sat' in solvers.py (discrete domains: enum, money, date-as-ordered-int).
conflicts() operation — minimal violated rule subset (unsat-core 'why not').
Typed autovar over domains rather than only real-valued quantities with units.

precondition_checks: conditional rules (if LCL vs FCL, customs window differs) as disjunctions

out_of_scope: fully autonomous production action-gating enforcement (infra beyond proof layer)

scenarios.plain: Ship from BLR to DUB, hazmat true, budget cap 8200 USD, deadline 2026-09-04. Agent claims route carrier B to warehouse WH-DUB-2. Prove every rule holds, or name the violated ones.
scenarios.note: Plain-text scenario is committed as the design contract. When the logistics grammar ships, this becomes a runnable operation. The verification surface is: derive(route) over conjunction of hardcoded rules; unsatisfiable -> conflicts() returns minimal violated set, never a bool.

scenarios.plain: Does projected net gain over a horizon satisfy an accounting invariant (sum of monthly flows balances, no negative balance without authorized credit)?
scenarios.note: Finance wants numeric+ledger invariants. Same conjunction engine; extensions: money arithmetic exactness, audit-trail lineage. Not started.

decisions.title: Operations is the next family, Z3-gated
decisions.decision: logistics/finance grammars are stubs until Z3 backend lands.
decisions.rationale: Discrete satisfiability (the entire value here) is not expressible with the current sympy/algebra backend. Z3 is a hard prerequisite, not a nice-to-have.

decisions.title: Agent cannot write rules in this family either
decisions.decision: Rules (delivers_by, within_budget, hazmat_compat, warehouse_serves) are hardcoded grammar. Agent supplies only facts (givens/claims).
decisions.rationale: Rule fabrication by the agent would void the proof. Same invariant as dec-002.

known_gaps: No Z3 backend (blocks everything in this family).
Typed-domain autovar (enum/money/date) not implemented in model.py.
conflicts() operation has no shipped contract example yet — SCHEMA.md section 3 lists it, but a worked trace is pending Z3.

out_of_scope.claim: statistical risk scoring replacing deterministic rule satisfaction
out_of_scope.why: risk as a number is judgment; rule satisfaction is proof. Both can exist, statistical is not v1.

out_of_scope.claim: acting on the verdict (blocking an agent's action in prod)
out_of_scope.why: the proof layer delivers the verdict; enforcement is downstream infra.
